classification.difficultyReason: Choose one journey distance as the unknown, express the other as 25 minus that distance, and convert both distances to times before adding them. This links the taught journey model and time formula, followed by routine linear solving.

content.prompt: Luisa travels 25 km in $3\frac34$ hours. She walks part of the way at 4 km/h and cycles the rest at 12 km/h. How far did she walk?

answer.short:
10 km.

Use time = distance ÷ speed for each part of the journey.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ km be the distance Luisa walks. She cycles $(25-x)$ km. Using time = distance ÷ speed,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x}{4}+\frac{25-x}{12}&=\frac{15}{4}\\3x+25-x&=45\\2x+25&=45\\2x&=20\\x&=10\end{align*}$$
Luisa walked 10 km.
